jsp-likely-xss.message: Detected a XSS vulnerability $VAR is rendered unsafely in template

potential-symlink-takeover-with-os.execu.message: os.Executable()s behaviour varies between operating systems. On Linux symlinks are followed, while on MacOS and Windows they are not. Depending on context, this could lead to file replacement attacks and local privilege escalation.

sprintf-unescaped-control-characters.message: fmt.Sprintf()'s %s formatting verb does not escape control characters in a string, such as \u000a or backtick-enclosed multilines. This could lead to various vulnerabilities such as header injection, request smuggling, log injection, etc.

non-atomic-use-of-converted-uintptr.message: An unsafe.Pointer converted to an uintptr must be used in an atomic step. Without this it is not guaranteed that the memory location uintptr points to will contain the intended structure.

jakarta-mail-internetaddress-overloaded-.message: InternetAddress(String, ...) constructors do NOT validate the email address. They assign the address field directly. Prefer the single-arg constructor + explicit validation.

jakarta-mail-internetaddress-single-arg-.message: new InternetAddress(String) parses an email for RFC compliance, but should not be treated as a full security/identity check. Ensure domain checks and trust decisions are not based solely on constructor success.

jakarta-mail-mimemessage-raw-envelope-ct.message: MimeMessage constructed from a raw source or InputStream. Headers such as From, Reply-To, Subject, and Newsgroups will be parsed using InternetAddress/NewsAddress. Ensure user-controlled envelopes are canonicalized and not blindly trusted.

jakarta-mail-mimemessage-newsgroups-reci.message: MimeMessage.getRecipients(Message.RecipientType.NEWSGROUPS) used. Newsgroups headers may be concatenated and parsed via NewsAddress, which silently normalizes malformed values. Review how this data is used.

spring-internetaddresseditor-usage.message: Spring InternetAddressEditor used. This relies on Jakarta Mail parsing and will decode encoded personal names (RFC 2047). Ensure the resulting personal/name fields are not used as trust signals.

spring-simplemailmessage-setfrom-raw.message: SimpleMailMessage.setFrom(...) called. If the from-address is influenced by user input, be aware of encoded names and complex email syntax (e.g. encoded words, group addresses, angle-bracket forms).

email-domain-split-index.message: Domain derived via email.split("@")[1]. This is fragile for complex, RFC-compliant addresses (e.g. "\"foo@bar.com\"@example.com"). Prefer a proper email parser and canonicalization for domain checks.

email-domain-lastindexof.message: Domain derived via substring(lastIndexOf("@") + 1). This can be tricked by overloaded or encoded email addresses. Prefer a proper parser and canonical form instead of manual substring logic.

email-domain-endswith.message: Domain/tenant derived using email.endsWith("..."). This can be bypassed with addresses like tester@evil.com@trusted.com. Prefer comparing the canonical domain returned by a parser.

hibernate-email-annotation-field.message: Field annotated with @Email. The default Hibernate validator is not RFC 2047-aware and can accept complex syntax (e.g. "\"foo@bar.com\"@example.com"). Review any domain or trust logic that uses this field (split/substring/endsWith).

gcm-static-iv.message: GCM IV and key are both same source $KEY_BYTES

randomstringutils-insecure-rng.message: RandomStringUtils uses java.util.Random by default which is not suitable for security

UnsafeHttpInvokerServiceExporter-extends.message: Unsafe Spring Service Exporter $CLASS extends RemoteInvocationSerializingExporter

php-filter-chain-read-from-oracle.message: Detected possible file read caused by the the error-based oracle of PHP filter chains. It can be used to leak the content of a local file when passed to vulnerable functions even when the server does not return the file content.

allow-privilege-escalation.message: Container $NAME allows for privilege escalation via setuid or setgid binaries. Add 'allowPrivilegeEscalation: false' in 'securityContext' to prevent this.

no-security-context.message: Container allows for running applications as root. This can result in privilege escalation attacks. Add 'runAsNonRoot: true' in 'securityContext' to prevent this.

run-as-non-root-unsafe-value.message: Container allows for running applications as root. This can result in privilege escalation attacks. Change 'runAsNonRoot:' to 'true' in 'securityContext' to prevent this.

run-as-non-root.message: Container allows for running applications as root. This can result in privilege escalation attacks. Add 'runAsNonRoot: true' in 'securityContext' to prevent this.
